grounding.supports: Permit-authoritative TDS reporting: discharge and intake weekly values must be reported as geometric means; net TDS is a derived difference (*8), not a raw single-sample scalar.
TDS discharge/intake rows are report-only; TDS net-increase rows carry numeric concentration limits enforceable separately from weekly grab semantics.

Excursion/violation evidence is tied to named aggregate statistics reported on the DMR (30-day average, monthly average, weekly average, etc.), not to undifferentiated individual monitoring samples by default.
Enforceable TDS net-incremental increase limit is framed as a 30-day average, consistent with aggregated comparison rather than single-sample comparison.
Structured limit rows for parameter 70295 link geometric-mean reporting comment to AVG statistical-base numeric limits at weekly monitoring frequency.
Negative: the same schedule-level DMR comment text does not establish schedule-wide geometric-mean comparison blocking for BOD, pH, and other non-TDS parameters.

interpretation: tds_aggregated_reporting (scoped): For TDS limits governed by footnotes *6–*8, weekly measurements must be aggregated (geometric mean of weekly values) for reporting; the enforceable TDS net-increase numeric limit is a 30-day average, so individual weekly samples are not the comparison unit for limit exceedance. The geometric-mean comment does not impose schedule-wide comparison blocking on non-TDS parameters sharing the schedule-level comment text.
remaining_uncertainty: The workspace lacks weekly sub-period DMR rows, so it cannot verify that monthly reported scalars equal geometric means of weekly samples or the permit's unstated formula linking weekly geometric means to the 30-day-average net-increase limit used for enforcement.
